MK: Asthma exacerbation due to air pollution related to wildfire- known history of intermittent asthma, and sensitivity to environmental smoke. No chest pain, no recent tobacco use, no fever or chills, and nonproductive cough. Symptoms are worse when outdoors and exposed to smoke from wildfires which have been more intense and longer lasting than in the past. Higher amounts of particulate in the atmosphere and sustained smoke in air are provoking her symptoms. She gets some relief with avoiding outside air and the use of an albuterol inhaler. Physical exam reveals wheezing and diminished peak flow from baseline.

* Bronchitis: remote history of tobacco but no fever or significant sputum production.
* COPD: remote history of tobacco but no significant sputum production. Baseline spirometry not consistent with COPD (FEV1 >80%, FEV1/FVC ratio > 70%).
* Pneumonia: no fever, chills, improves indoors and with inhaler, no significant sputum production

Patient Education

* Educate on use of peak flow meter and determine an Asthma Action Plan
* Discuss avoidance of exertion and reduction of outdoor activity such as gardening on poor air quality days
* Recognize that these environmental events which have been in existence are now more intense and will be a recurrent problem
* Monitor daily Air Quality Index, outdoor avoidance if >100
* Direct patient to an inexpensive mask that will filter pollen and particulates. Need N-95 non-medical grade masks which are available at hardware and home improvement stores or high-quality filters for home HVAC which can filter damaging fine particles Need to assure fit.
* Advise patient that although environmental conditions are more severe, they are seasonal, so outdoor activity restrictions are time bound. Ongoing monitoring of air quality will be required.
* Recognize emotional distress provoked by wildfire and climate conditions and provide a referral for social work and community services to address medication needs, grocery delivery and emotional support through behavioral health providers or support groups
* Provide contact for the national Disaster Distress Helpline, which provides counseling for people experiencing emotional distress related to human caused or natural disasters.
